items.title: Reggie Watkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, May 22, 2018
items.q: I had the incredible opportunity to play and back up Oliver Lake.

ctx.x: It goes back to, you were taking about trad jazz. I think that it doesn’t rate that high in jazz history or in academia, because it’s too darn happy. It doesn’t sound like serious enough to study.

Right. And that’s debatable. And you mentioned to me before Branford Marsalis. I went to a Branford Marsalis lecture a few weeks ago at the University of Pittsburgh. And it was interesting. He pointed out that he has, you know, a student that wants to play like John Coltrane and is just listening only to John Coltrane. And he said, “How do you think he got to play that way? Do you think he sat and listened to albums of his future self and transcribed it?” He said, “You’ve got to listen to the people — who was…

together and I had no business being on the stage with Oliver Lake but I was thrilled. And we were tasked to put together a set list. He said to us, he said he didn’t know any standards. He didn’t know the American Songbook. He didn’t know things like, just things that you would think a jazz musician would know. But he did know some things like Eric Dolphy tunes and so I don’t think he would be somebody, and I might be wrong about this but I wouldn’t guess he’s somebody that’s versed in twenties and thirties…
